study: Murphy, Weinhardt & Wyness 2021 (peer observation/Lesson Study RCT, 181 schools, Econ Educ Rev 82; CEP DP 1565 / ERIC ED593175)
delivery_evidence: All participating teachers received five full in-person training days held by external educational experts (Edge Hill University), and the intervention itself is in-person peer-to-peer classroom lesson observation and feedback (18 observations over 2 years); no online delivery (Intervention section; 'all participating teachers received five full training days held by educational experts').
test_alignment_evidence: Included outcomes are national, compulsory, externally-marked KS2 (age-11) tests (maths, reading, SPAG; primary = combined maths+reading composite), broad independent standardized assessments; the teacher-assessed science measure is researcher_made and would be filtered (Table 4, PDF p.35).
curriculum_evidence: Intervention is a peer observation/feedback (Lesson Study) programme aimed at improving teaching practice with no new curriculum/materials; control schools 'did not receive any information about the treatment or training materials' (Method; intervention = peer-to-peer observation and feedback, no curriculum provided).
outcome_timing_evidence: KS2 outcomes were taken one year after the intervention ended (pupils tested at age 11, a year after the 2-year programme); the extracted full-dose (cohort 2) and cohort-1 waves are both post-intervention follow-ups (abstract/results; 'national tests a year after the program ended'; Table 4 panels).
